articles.body: Dominik Livakovic se queda en el Barça. El veterano meta croata formará parte de la plantilla de Hansi Flick para la temporada 26-27. El club catalán tiene el margen de fair play necesario para inscribirlo este martes y el cancerbero no tendrá que irse cedido a otra entidad. Livakovic fichó por el Barcelona la semana pasada, el 27 de agosto y se vinculó por cuatro campañas, hasta junio de 2030. El club catalán cerró el traspaso con el Fenerbache en dos millones de euros más medio en variables. Pero su continuidad en el Spotify Camp Nou no estaba asegurada ya que dependía de si había suficiente fair play para anotar su nombre en LaLiga. Y lo hay, de ahí que vaya a ser inscrito en unos minutos. El arquero, de 31 años, será el segundo portero del Barcelona este curso. El primero es Joan García. Szczesny será el tercero. Este verano han salido Ter Stegen, cedido al Ajax, e Iñaki Peña, traspasado al Panathinaikos. El arquero internacional tiene una dilatada trayectoria. Disputó, por ejemplo, 310 encuentros con el Dinamo de Zagreb, 108 con el NK Zagreb, 74 con el Fenerbache... además militó en la filas del Girona, estuvo cedido unos meses en la campaña 25-26, aunque no intervino en ningún encuentro con el equipo de Montilivi. Por otro lado, el Barça también inscribirá a Brian Fariñas, centrocampista del filial que estaba trabajando de forma habitual con los de Flick. articles.title: Iliman Ndiaye: Manchester City sign winger from Everton for £65m
articles.summary: Manchester City sign winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton in a deal worth up to £65m.
articles.body:
Iliman Ndiaye's journey to Manchester City has been something of a scenic route after he completed a move to Etihad Stadium from Everton in a deal worth up to £65m.

The deadline day move for the Senegal winger, 26, is worth £60m plus a further £5m in add-ons - a little over six years since he made his professional debut playing in the seventh tier of English football.

"I've worked my whole life for an opportunity like this," said Ndiaye, who has signed a five-year contract with the club.

"City are one of the best clubs in the world and I've seen them win everything as I've grown up. To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I'm determined to grab it with both hands."

Ndiaye had held talks with Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal earlier in the summer while Tottenham had agreed terms with Everton on Friday night for Ndiaye, when it looked as though Richarlison would move the other way in a separate transfer.

However, sources indicated Richarlison failed to agree personal terms with his former club and as a result, Spurs were unable to proceed with the Ndiaye transfer.

The move comes on the same day City agreed to pay a joint-British transfer record fee of £125m for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

The Argentian international is set to become City's eighth summer arrival with Enzo Maresca's side having also signed Elliot Anderson, Geronimo Rulli, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Allan Elias, Jeremy Monga and Pierce Charles.

Ndiaye's journey from non-league football to City

As a 19-year-old living in London, Ndiaye was in the youth ranks of Boreham Wood and playing Sunday league football when he was invited for a one-week trial with Sheffield United.

Two trial games were enough for the then-Premier League club to sign the talented teenager, although it would be another 18 months until he made an appearance for the Blades.

Instead, he spent the second half of the 2019-20 campaign on loan at Hyde United in the Northern Premier Division, six levels below the top division.

He made six appearances in his very first taste of professional football, often risking missing the last train back to Sheffield to stay out on the training pitch.

"It's not always been easy in my career," said Ndiaye.

"But I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I'm here."

After returning to Bramall Lane, Ndiaye made his Premier League debut in March 2021 against Leicester City but it would be another three-and-a-half years until he became established at the highest level following the Blades' relegation.

Two seasons in the Championship culminated in Ndiaye spearheading their return to the top flight in 2023 with 14 goals in 43 starts but he was then sold to Marseille that summer.

Ndiaye struggled during a season in France before joining Everton for an initial £16m fee in July 2024.

A firm fan favourite on Merseyside, "Skiliman" scored 15 goals and provided four assists in 67 Premier League games for the Toffees before his City move.

In a summer of highly-inflated transfer fees, value has become increasingly hard to determine.

On one hand, the Senegal international is a player of superlative skill, evasive, quick and wonderfully entertaining with the ball at his feet.

Ndiaye was responsible for 73 of Everton 's 250 completed dribbles last season, the highest share of any Premier League player.

Everton fans may also point to recent moves in the Premier League involving City, such as the sale of Savio to Tottenham for an initial £75m, as further evidence that the club should have demanded more for Ndiaye.

On the other hand, Everton are effectively quadrupling the initial £16m they paid Marseille to sign Ndiaye two years ago for a player whose underlying numbers, at this stage at least, are not truly elite.

In the Premier League last season, Ndiaye only ranked joint third at Everton alone for goal contributions (nine), with Beto (10) and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (12) providing more.

It is reasonable to assume that those numbers for Ndiaye will improve in a more attacking team at City but his general creativity is also middling as things stand.

He created 36 chances in total in the Premier League last season, ranking him only fourth at Everton . Toffees midfielder James Garner created 26 more. Jack Grealish, whose season ended in January because of injury, created eight more.

Grealish has effectively replaced Ndiaye at Everton following his loan move from Enzo Maresca's side.

Casting the net a little wider, 45 Premier League players have recorded more goal contributions than Ndiaye's 19 since he made his Everton debut two years ago.

As a 26-year-old set to be surrounded by better players, it would be no surprise should his numbers flourish at the Etihad.

But even in today's money, £65m for Ndiaye's current output may not be as questionable a deal as it sounds.

articles.title: Chelsea agree £47.1m move for Monaco's Lamine Camara
articles.summary: Chelsea have moved to replace outgoing midfielder Enzo Fernandez with Monaco's Lamine Camara.
articles.body:
Chelsea have agreed a £47.1m deal to sign Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

The 22-year-old is set to undergo a medical after Chelsea complete the sale of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a deal that matched the £125m British transfer record .

Chelsea had been reluctant to complete a transfer for Monaco's asking price but they are believed to have dropped their demands when striker Folarin Balogun's move to Everton from the French club came into renewed doubt.

It was expected the Blues would continue with their current midfielder options despite sanctioning Fernandez's exit but an opportunity to sign one of their primary targets at a lower price was taken up.

They had also held talks with Roma's Manu Kone and another unnamed Premier League option.

The signing is not viewed as a like-for-like replacement for Fernandez, with Camara offering a different profile in midfield. However, Chelsea believe the deal will help maintain the strength of new manager Xabi Alonso's squad.

One of the club's aims this summer was to emerge from the transfer window with a stronger squad despite selling Fernandez to a direct rival.

Chelsea believe they have achieved that after signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa in a club-record £117m deal, centre-back Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace and, most recently, goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa .

The club have also recruited strikers Emmanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck, winger Geovany Quenda, midfielders Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco, as well as full-backs Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria.

Alonso's side have won all three of their matches this season, beating Fulham and Brighton in the Premier League, and have also reached the third round of the Carabao Cup with victory over Luton Town.

Chelsea have agreed a £47.1m deal to sign Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

The 22-year-old is set to undergo a medical after Chelsea complete the sale of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a deal that matched the £125m British transfer record .

Chelsea had been reluctant to complete a transfer for Monaco's asking price but they are believed to have dropped their demands when striker Folarin Balogun's move to Everton from the French club came into renewed doubt.

It was expected the Blues would continue with their current midfielder options despite sanctioning Fernandez's exit but an opportunity to sign one of their primary targets at a lower price was taken up.

They had also held talks with Roma's Manu Kone and another unnamed Premier League option.

The signing is not viewed as a like-for-like replacement for Fernandez, with Camara offering a different profile in midfield. However, Chelsea believe the deal will help maintain the strength of new manager Xabi Alonso's squad.

One of the club's aims this summer was to emerge from the transfer window with a stronger squad despite selling Fernandez to a direct rival.

Chelsea believe they have achieved that after signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa in a club-record £117m deal, centre-back Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace and, most recently, goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa.

The club have also recruited strikers Emmanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck, winger Geovany Quenda, midfielders Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco, as well as full-backs Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria.

Alonso's side have won all three of their matches this season, beating Fulham and Brighton in the Premier League, and have also reached the third round of the Carabao Cup with victory over Luton Town.

articles.title: Official: Barcelona announce another deadline day exit
articles.summary: La Liga giants Barcelona have on Tuesday announced the departure of another highly-regarded young member of the club’s reserve team ranks.This comes amid con...
articles.body:
La Liga giants Barcelona have on Tuesday announced the departure of another highly-regarded young member of the club's reserve team ranks.

This comes amid confirmation of Toni Fernández taking his talents to Italy, to link up with Serie A outfit Venezia.

18-year-old Toni's name had emerged as a prominent one in the transfer chatter surrounding Barcelona in the buildup to deadline day. After the starlet was forced to face up to his first-team path being yet further blocked by the signings of Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi, Toni and his entourage began seeking out the best landing spot to further his development.

From here, the aforementioned Venezia entered the scene, promising the versatile attacker a prominent place in their senior setup this coming season.

And such promises evidently proved enough to convince Toni of the merits of a move to the Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo. As per a statement across Barcelona's website and social media platforms on Tuesday evening:

'FC Barcelona and Venezia FC have reached an agreement for the transfer of Toni Fernández. FC Barcelona retain a buy-back option and a percentage of any future sale.

'FC Barcelona would like to wish Toni Fernández the best of luck in this new chapter and thank him for his dedication throughout all these years at the Club.'

Toni's Blaugrana departure comes just hours on from that of cousin and close friend Guille, who has linked up with RCD Mallorca in Spanish football's 2nd tier.

articles.title: Iliman Ndiaye transfer news: Man City complete £65m deal for Everton winger as Cody Gakpo alternative
articles.summary: Manchester City have completed the £65m signing of winger Iliman Ndiaye; City had an £80m bid for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo rejected on Monday and moved for Ndiaye as an alternative; Jack Grealish set to join Everton on loan with Toffees making an offer for Man Utd's Joshua Zirkzee
articles.body:
The deal comprises a £60m guaranteed payment plus £5m in bonuses.

Ndiaye, who had also been wanted by Tottenham, has signed a five-year contract at Manchester City.

Jack Grealish is set to go the other way in a separate deal after he was given permission to have an Everton medical, with a season-long loan deal agreed that covers the final year of his Manchester City contract.

Sky Sports News also learned Everton have made an offer for Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee .

Ndiaye's City arrival comes after Liverpool rejected Manchester City's £80m bid for Cody Gakpo.

Sky Sports News understands Liverpool were concerned about their chances of bringing in a replacement for the Dutchman.

Manchester City wanted to sign a wide forward and a central midfielder before the window closes, with the club agreeing a joint-British record deal for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez on Deadline Day.

City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham earlier this month, reducing Enzo Maresca's options on the wing.

City did not name a winger on their bench in Friday's win over Crystal Palace and started with Phil Foden - who Enzo Maresca admitted is not a winger - out wide at Selhurst Park.

Ndiaye, who becomes Manchester City's seventh summer signing, said: "I've worked my whole life for an opportunity like this.

"City are one of the best clubs in the world and I've seen them win everything as I've grown up.

"To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I'm determined to grab it with both hands.

"It's not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes, and now I'm here. It feels so good.

"I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That's why I know this is the perfect fit."

Manchester City director of football Hugo Viana added: "Iliman is a very talented footballer. He's had to work incredibly hard to reach this level and in my first conversation with him it was immediately obvious how grounded he is and the determination he has to be the best player he can be.

"I've no doubt City fans will get a thrill seeing him in action for us."

articles.title: Mykhailo Mudryk transfer: Tottenham sign Chelsea winger on loan
articles.summary: Tottenham sign Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk on loan until the end of the season.
articles.body:
Tottenham have signed Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk on loan until the end of the season.

As part of the agreement, Spurs have the option to turn the 25-year-old Ukraine international's move permanent for £75m.

Mudryk resolved a doping case with the Football Association last month, but has not played a competitive match since November 2024.

Chelsea had been in talks with Leeds and rejected at least one offer, but Spurs entered the race at a late stage after failing in attempts to sign Iliman Ndiaye, who has since joined Manchester City from Everton , and Liverpool attacker Cody Gakpo.

Mudryk took part in Chelsea 's pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, where he made his return in a friendly against Juventus in Hong Kong.

However, he was not included in Xabi Alonso's squad for the Premier League victories against Fulham and Brighton , or the Carabao Cup win against Luton.

Mudryk scored 10 goals and provided 11 assists in 73 games in all competitions for Chelsea .

articles.title: Lamine Camara: Chelsea agree £47m deal to sign Monaco midfielder as Enzo Fernandez replacement
articles.summary: Chelsea are looking for a midfield addition with Enzo Fernandez set to join Manchester City in a £125m deal, which is a joint-record for a British club; Camara, 22, has been at Monaco for two years since joining from Metz in 2024
articles.body:
He is set to sign a six-year deal pending a medical. Monaco rejected a £38.5m (€45m) bid from Chelsea earlier on Deadline Day.

Roma's Manu Kone was also shortlisted as a potential option, while Chelsea are also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

Camara has spent the last two years at Monaco having joined from Metz in 2024.

Manchester City have agreed a deal with Chelsea to sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m.

The deal matches the British record transfer fee Liverpool paid for Newcastle striker Alexander Isak during last year's summer Deadline Day.

Chelsea will make a £18m profit on the midfielder they signed for £107m three-and-a-half years ago.

Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como .

The goalkeeper had been bumped down to Stamford Bridge following the arrival of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa .

Elsewhere, midfielder Dario Essugo has completed a season-long loan move to sister club Strasbourg . Essugo was of interest to Hull in this window.

Striker Deivid Washington has completed a permanent transfer to Strasbourg. He signed from Santos for £17.1m three years ago but made only three appearances.

Forward Dujuan Richards has also joined Wimbledon on a season-long loan.

Meanwhile, Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka has arrived in Glasgow ahead of his loan move to Celtic, who are also working to finalise a deal for Chelsea left-back Landon Emenalo.

articles.title: Sheffield United 3-2 Bolton: Romelle Donovan scores stoppage-time winner for Blades
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Bolton Wanderers at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night; Romelle Donovan scores late winner in five-goal thriller for Chris Wilder's Blades.
articles.body:
Xavier Simons struck inside the opening minute and Sam Dalby was also on target for the visitors, but United twice hit back to level with goals from Japhet Tanganga and Patrick Bamford before Donovan's dramatic goal secured all three points for Chris Wilder's men.

The visitors got off to a flying start, scoring with only 23 seconds on the clock. Thierry Gale broke down the left and advanced into the area before firing in a shot which was blocked, with Simons seizing on the rebound and hooking the ball into the net.

United responded soon afterwards, levelling in the fourth minute when Sydie Peck's free kick was met by Tanganga, whose far-post header crept just inside Jack Bonham's right-hand post.

That set the tone for the rest of the half with the home side dominating and going close to taking the lead on several occasions.

Chris Forino came to Bolton's rescue when Bamford looked set to score, producing a superb goal-line clearance to keep the striker's shot out.

Bamford also failed to get a proper connection to a low cross from Ben Brereton-Diaz, screwing his shot wide, while Peck's shot fizzed over the bar and Donovan fired off target.

Bolton went close soon after the re-start when Gale's low shot was touched wide by Michael Cooper. John McAtee also had a chance to put them back in front, shooting a fraction wide.

The visitors regained the lead in the 67th minute when Gale's cross from the left found Dalby, who planted a header past Cooper after getting between two defenders.

Bamford made it 2-2 a minute later, stabbing in from close range after Sam McCallum did well on the left and played the ball across the face of goal.

The home side rode their luck at times with Cooper kept busy as Bolton enjoyed a good spell.

It took an important save from Cooper to keep the scores level, turning McAtee's downward header onto the bar. The keeper also got down smartly to his left to keep out Josh Sheehan's firm drive and then did well to tip over Samuel Iling-Junior's effort from inside the area.

Then, in the third minute of time added on, a ball from Kalvin Phillips picked out Donovan, who strode into the area before beating Bonham with a shot which struck the roof of the net.

articles.title: Swansea 2-0 Watford: Ji-Sung Eom and Adam Idah net in Swans win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and Watford at the Swansea.com Stadium on Tuesday night; Ji-Sung Eom and Adam Idah score as Vitor Matos' in-form Swans earn another win.
articles.body:
Adam Idah and Eom Ji-sung grabbed first-half goals as Swansea made it 10 points from four games, leapfrogging Charlton and Wolves to take over at the summit.

It also meant Watford lost their unbeaten league record after beating Southampton and drawing against Wrexham and West Ham.

Watford showed plenty of intent throughout but were unable to remedy the situation after a difficult opening half-hour in which Swansea oozed confidence and class.

Before kick-off paid Swansea tribute to their former manager Kenny Jackett, who died in June at the age of 64.

Jackett spent his entire playing career at Watford with 428 appearances for the Hornets and his family were in attendance at Swansea.com Stadium.

Swansea were impressive from the off, with Idah testing Federico Ravaglia and Marko Stamenic heading against a post, with Joseph Opoku unable to force the ball home in a desperate scramble almost on the goal-line.

The visitors' defence was breached after eight minutes when Stephen Eustaquio, on his home debut after arriving from Porto, released Idah and he had presence of mind to give Eom a tap-in for his second goal in as many games.

Watford cleared their heads for Mattie Pollock and Hector Kyprianou to go close, but Swansea doubled their advantage after 29 minutes.

This time Eom was the creator, cutting in from the left-hand touchline and finding Idah with a delicious reverse pass.

Idah steadied himself as Ravaglia approached and slipped the ball through the goalkeeper's legs with the minimum of fuss.

Watford hinted at a way back into the contest as Mamadou Doumbia sent a header over and Kyprianou did not get enough purchase on his, and the Hornets also started the second half well.

Swansea should have extended their lead when Melker Wildell fed Eom, but this time the South Korean lacked conviction and Ravaglia rushed out to avert the danger.

Idah's work-rate was to be admired and the Republic of Ireland striker left the action midway through the second period to a rousing ovation.

Zan Vipotnik replaced Idah, with last season's Championship top scorer seemingly set to stay at Swansea after summer speculation that he was to leave the club.

Wildell whistled a shot past a post, while Edoardo Bove led a Hornets' breakout at the other end for Edo Kayembe to blaze over.

The cherry on the Swansea cake was almost applied 10 minutes from time after more slick passing from Vitor Matos' side found Wildell in a central position 20 yards out.

Wildell's ferocious strike seemed to be arrowing in, but Ravaglia stuck out a strong right hand to deny the Sweden international his first Swansea goal.
